key_idea: Adding a repeatedly to b walks b through the coset b + <gcd(a,10)> mod 10, so a digit coprime to 10 (1,3,7) can eliminate every other digit; the only question is whether such a unit exists or can be manufactured.
sketch: If any digit is 1, 3 or 7, use it to kill all others: answer 1 (the last digit can never be eliminated). If there is a 5 and a nonzero even digit, a unit can be built: 5+2=7, 5+6=1, 5+8=3, and with 4s either 5+4=9 directly (n=2) or 4+4=8 then 5+8=3 (a second 4 can be made by adding 4 onto a 0 or onto 5+5=0). Otherwise the multiset is all even (parity invariant, 9 unreachable) or only 0s and 5s (closed under addition), so nothing can be removed and the answer is n. O(n). Verified against a BFS over all multisets with n<=5.
